answer.evidence: The tower is a flat front view, 12 px wide in rows 0-26 and 14 px wide at the base in rows 27-31. The top is a 3-row gradient band (rows 1-3, L 169, 202, 244) followed by a darker row 4 (L 144). This reads as a bevelled front-facing cornice with a highlight, not a foreshortened horizontal top, so I count only about 2 rows of top or rim. Rows 5-22 are vertical shelf faces with glasses (black, brown, red and blue frames) separated by 1-row light dividers. Rows 23-26 are a glass-fronted case. The base in rows 27-31 repeats the same gradient strip with no top surface. Nothing in the drawing shows a top at depth, an ellipse, or a receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall, narrow white/grey kiosk with a small colored grid of items. It has about 3 lightness steps on the body (white face, light grey, dark grey frame). The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black/grey line around the whole shape. That is the sticker look, unlike the tinted material-tone outlines of the hedge (0% neutral), the cheese stall (1%) and the roofed well (33%). Measured tones per tile are 11, comparable to the hedge (9) but below the stall (17) and well (20). Flat coverage is 0%, but the body is smooth and lacks grain, plaster speckle or per-material shading. The lamp reference is also neutral-outlined, but it is a thin object, so it is not a fair comparison for a bulky prop. Beside the richly shaded stall and well, the candidate reads thinner, flatter and more sticker-like, with shallow ramps and a neutral outline.

answer.evidence: The tower is a flat front view: every row from 0 to 26 has the same width of 12, with a wider 14-px base at rows 27-31. Rows 1-4 form a header strip with a gradient (a6a9ad, c6cad4, f3f4f7, then a darker 8d9095 at row 4). Row 5 directly below it is light, with no eave shadow, so the strip reads as a front-facing cornice and not a receding top plane. The base rows 28-30 repeat the same gradient, which is another front-facing strip. Rows 5-26 are a vertical face of shelves holding eyewear in brown, red and blue, with a mirror or window at rows 23-26. There is no ellipse, no sloped roof, no visible contents from above and no receding side face. At most a 1-2 row rim is present, so the front face dominates.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow grey-white display tower with a uniform dark neutral outline. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, while the stall, hedge and well references are tinted (0-33%). The body has only about 3 lightness steps (white face, light grey side, dark grey edge). The small coloured eyewear squares are tiny flat dots with no per-item shading. It has no grain, speckle or material texture, so it reads as a flat sticker next to the references' tile scallops, plank grain and leaf clumps. The measured facts do not rescue it. Its 11 visible tones per tile are in the range of the hedge (9) but below the stall (17) and well (20), and it has only 15 distinct colours in total against 38-40 for the stall and well. The 0% near-flat coverage comes from the busy shelf pattern, not from real shading depth. The neutral black-grey outline and the shallow ramps make it fall short of the Beodeul standard.

answer.evidence: The top cap spans rows 1-4. Row 1 is mid grey, row 2 lighter, row 3 is the lightest row and works as the front-edge line, and row 4 is a darker grey shadow row. A shelf line at row 5 follows, then the front face with shelves of sunglasses from rows 6 to 26. Rows 27-31 are a slightly wider base. The top is only 3 rows, but it has an edge line and a shadow row, so it is marginal but passes as a top surface. The front face is clearly more than 3 rows tall, and there is no side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, tall kiosk drawn in a grey-white body with a dark neutral outline and a few small coloured product dots. All of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), which gives the black-line sticker look; the cheese stall and well references have tinted outlines (1% and 33% neutral) and the hedge has 0%. The body is built from about 3 lightness steps (white, light grey, dark grey), against the 5-6 steps the references use for each material. The 11 visible tones per tile are comparable to the hedge's 9, but they come mostly from the small coloured dots rather than from shaded material ramps. The stall (17) and well (20) are clearly richer, with per-plank, per-tile and per-stone shading, whereas the candidate has no grain, bevel or material texture on its panel. Near-flat coverage is 0%, but only because the panel is tiny and busy with dots. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.
